crime: A girl made a card by the lounge fireplace for every girl's special day, a surprise passed round for all to sign. {WITCH_NAME}, who cut the paper beside her, had told her alone that her father walked out eight years ago this week, and asked her to keep it secret.
On the anniversary evening, the girl gathered the others at the fire, told them, and had each sign a card. She handed it to {WITCH_NAME} before them all: "We're all here for you."

Eight years ago, the morning after {WITCH_NAME} whispered her father had left, a teacher had the whole class sign a card and read it aloud while {WITCH_NAME} stood at the front holding it: "We're all here for you."
{WITCH_NAME} smiled and told the girl it was fine. "Once you tell one person, everyone already knows."
After the others left, she looked at the card and her Magic showed it curling black in the flames. She dropped it in unread.

At quarter past five the next evening, the girl was on the hearth beneath the mantel sword, tying a ribbon round a new card. {WITCH_NAME} strangled her with it, moved the sword onto a worn hook, and watched the hook until she saw when it would give: ten past six. At half past five she sat down in the dining hall, saying the girl was finishing a card, and never left the others' sight again.

At ten past six, a clang of steel brought the prisoners running. They found the girl strangled on the hearth, the sword fallen across her open hand, a cut in her palm. In the trial court they decided she had grabbed the sword while fighting her strangler. That was the clang; {WITCH_NAME} had been at dinner with them.
A prisoner turned the cut palm up. It had never bled. They realized the girl had died before the sword fell on its own, at a minute only {WITCH_NAME}'s eyes could see coming.
fields.epitaph: She saw how the card would end. Never what was written inside.
execution: The execution stand raised a giant card, standing open. She stood against its blank inner page beneath a rack of giant pens. The pens signed name after name across the page around her, and the first two full stops pinned her sleeves to the paper. She looked up at the last pen's nib and saw it still whole long after she was gone. It wrote "We're all here for you" up to her chest and pressed the full stop. The nib sank in where the line ended. The pens lifted away, and she sagged still against the page, ringed by every name.

magic.name: The End in Sight
magic.text: She glimpses how and when any object or plant she looks at will finally break or wilt.
